answer_short.case-1: Chinese graphite goes in, and graphite goes out to five US battery and car makers. Who owns the plant isn't in the registry.
answer_short.case-2: BTR's 100% ownership is on record. The first graphite arrived from BTR's own Indonesian plant in Aug 2026, and nothing has been exported yet.
answer_short.case-3: The Oman plant isn't in the data yet. Zhongke graphite reaches the US today through Malaysian cell plants.
answer_short.case-4: Korean-owned, with Chinese graphite inputs. It sells to the same US buyers as BTR Indonesia.
answer_short.case-5: No Chinese-owned anode maker is shipping to the US from five corridors. Putailai's Malaysian plant is still being built.
answer_short.case-6: Chinese anode graphite goes in and finished cells go out to US buyers, from a plant owned by China's EVE Energy.
answer_short.case-7: Gotion's Chinese plants ship cells, packs and graphite to its US sites, but no US record shows who owns them.
answer_short.case-8: A non-Chinese chain from Mozambique to Louisiana, but the same mine also supplies Chinese-owned plants.

case-1.plant: PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material

chain.name: BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd.
chain.stake: Not in Sayari; one trade directory says 70%

chain.name: PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material

case-1.visibility: Ownership not visible in Sayari's registry data; rests on BTR's own statements.
case-1.inputs: Chinese artificial graphite (HS 3801) from BTR and a trader in the BTR Building; natural graphite from Mozambique, Madagascar and the UAE.
case-1.us_exposure: Ultium Cells (Warren, Spring Hill), SK Battery America, StarPlus Energy, General Motors, Tesla
questions: Ask the supplier for its shareholder register, filed with Indonesia's companies registry (AHU), and the identity of any minority shareholder.
Which graphite feedstock, and from which origin, went into the lots shipped to you? Ask for lot-level certificates.

case-2.status: Under construction; first graphite received Aug 2026

chain.name: BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd.

case-2.visibility: Visible in registry data at every step, 100% each time. One step joins two records of the Singapore holding company, and one matches BTR (Jiangsu)'s Singapore record to its Chinese record by name and address.
case-2.inputs: Construction goods from China, then 1,240 t of artificial graphite from BTR's Indonesian plant (19 Aug 2026).
case-2.us_exposure: None yet. Ford has been reported as an expected customer.
questions: Which of BTR's two Moroccan companies will run the anode line, and who owns the second one's Singapore parent (Rian International Holding)?
Where will the Tangier plant source its graphite and coke, and will any be Chinese-origin?

case-3.plant: Zhongke Xingcheng Sohar New Material Technology
case-3.visibility: Registry visible inside China; the Hong Kong and Oman steps rest on the company's filing.
case-3.inputs: None yet. Zhongke's Chinese plants already supply Malaysian cell makers.
case-3.us_exposure: Indirect today, through cells made in Malaysia (see Case 6).
questions: Once Sohar ships, does the shipper name the Oman project company or Zhongke Shinzoom (HK) Holdings?
Ask the supplier for its Omani commercial registration and shareholder certificate.

case-4.visibility: Visible in registry data; no Chinese owner among 50 ownership paths.
case-4.inputs: Chinese natural and spherical graphite from Qingdao suppliers (to Dec 2023 in the data; the company says it still uses some).
case-4.us_exposure: General Motors, SK Battery America, Tesla, Panasonic Energy, XALT; Ultium Cells by contract
questions: What share of the anode material you receive is made from Chinese-origin graphite, and who owns those graphite suppliers?
Which plant made your lots: Sejong (natural graphite) or Pohang (artificial graphite)?

case-5.visibility: Visible in registry data; Shanghai-based directors Han Zhongwei and Liu Fang.
questions: When Zichen Malaysia starts shipping, who are its buyers, and are any of them cell makers supplying the US?
Will the plant's graphite precursors (needle coke, petroleum coke) come from China?

case-6.visibility: Visible in registry data; the same directors (Liu Jincheng, Chan Tsun Ming) sit on both the Hong Kong and Malaysian boards.
case-6.inputs: Anode graphite from Zhongke Shinzoom, BTR, Shanshan and Qingdao Taidongrui; 91% of all inbound rows left from China.
case-6.us_exposure: EVE Energy North America, Briggs & Stratton, TTI, Milwaukee Tool, Stanley Black & Decker, Energizer and others
questions: Ask the cell supplier for its shareholder register and the ultimate parent's position on the US Section 1260H list.
Does the cell maker certify the origin and supplier of the anode material in your cells?

case-7.plant: Gotion, Inc. (Fremont, CA) and Gotion Illinois (Manteno, IL)

chain.name: Gotion High-Tech Co., Ltd.
chain.stake: Volkswagen (China) is a shareholder; % not shown

case-7.visibility: Visible from the Chinese side only; no US record lists shareholders.
case-7.inputs: Lithium-ion cells and packs from Gotion's Hefei and Tongcheng plants; 2 rows of artificial graphite (Dec 2025).
case-7.us_exposure: Gotion's own US entities; storage customers such as Richardson Electronics (announced partner)
questions: For US-assembled packs or storage systems, which cells are inside, and who made them?
Ask for the US entities' ownership certification under the prohibited-foreign-entity rules.

case-8.visibility: Partly visible in registry data; the percentages come from Syrah's own annual report.
case-8.inputs: Natural graphite from Syrah's Balama mine (Mozambique, 95% owned); some processing equipment and one small graphite lot from China.
questions: Confirm that the graphite in your lots came from Balama and not from third-party flake bought by Syrah Global.
The same mine sells to Chinese-owned plants. Make sure your contract covers chain-of-custody from mine to anode.

Chinese parent ownership of the transit.detected: Get the full shareholder chain to the ultimate owner, with percentages, and check each owner against the US prohibited-foreign-entity definitions.
Chinese parent ownership of the transit.suggested: Ownership rests on indirect evidence. Ask the supplier for a registry extract that names its shareholders.
Chinese parent ownership of the transit.not_visible: Ownership couldn't be confirmed. Ask for a registry extract and an ownership certification before relying on the supplier.
Chinese parent ownership of the transit.absent: No Chinese owner found. Keep a dated record of the ownership check and repeat it each year.

Same HS imported from China and exported.detected: The plant imports Chinese graphite and exports graphite to the US. Ask for lot-level origin certificates for the material you buy.
Same HS imported from China and exported.suggested: Inputs may include Chinese graphite. Ask what share of feedstock is Chinese-origin.
Same HS imported from China and exported.not_visible: Input origin couldn't be tested. Ask the supplier to list its graphite feedstock sources.
Same HS imported from China and exported.absent: No Chinese graphite inputs found in the data. Confirm with the supplier that this is still true.

Recent incorporation vs. first export da.detected: The company was set up shortly before exporting. Ask about its operating history and its real production capacity.
Recent incorporation vs. first export da.suggested: Check the incorporation date against first shipments.
Recent incorporation vs. first export da.not_visible: No incorporation date was available. Request the certificate of incorporation.
Recent incorporation vs. first export da.absent: Long operating history; no concern on this point.

Volume spike after a policy date.detected: Volumes changed after a policy date. Ask why, and whether the routing or product changed.
Volume spike after a policy date.not_visible: Not tested. Compare monthly volumes before and after July 2025 and March 2026.
Volume spike after a policy date.absent: No spike seen in the data.

Shared address or officer with a flagged.detected: The supplier shares an address or officer with a flagged company. Ask who the shared party is and what the relationship is.
Shared address or officer with a flagged.suggested: A possible shared officer or address. Confirm the relationship.
Shared address or officer with a flagged.absent: No shared address or officer with a flagged company found.

Entity-resolution fragmentation.detected: The supplier appears under several names. Agree with it the exact legal entity, registration number and address that should appear on your documents.
Entity-resolution fragmentation.suggested: Possible duplicate records. Confirm the legal entity.

Forced-labor / UFLPA sub-tier flags.detected: Sub-tier forced-labor flags appear. Request a supply-chain map to the mine or precursor level and check it against the UFLPA Entity List.
Forced-labor / UFLPA sub-tier flags.suggested: Possible sub-tier forced-labor exposure. Ask for a sub-tier supplier list.
